notes:
Endpoints (*Inventory → Endpoints*): a new section to document what connects to the network but is not network
gear: PCs, laptops, servers, virtual machines, printers, POS terminals, phones, mobiles, tablets, TVs, cameras, NAS
and IoT. Each endpoint has a location, company, manufacturer and model, serial number, asset tag, MAC, IP (linked to
IPAM), operating system, CPU, RAM and disk, assigned user, purchase date and warranty. Endpoints show up in the global
search, on each location's page and on the dashboard, and they do not count toward the license device limit.

Bulk edit: in the lists you can select several items (or every item that matches the filters) and move them to
another location, change their common fields or add and remove tags in one go.

Discovery (discovery module):

- Automatic classification of discovered hosts into 19 types (PC, printer, POS, phone, camera, access point, switch,
  firewall…) based on the manufacturer, open ports, name, SNMP, VLAN or prefix and LLDP/CDP capabilities, with a
  confidence level and "Why this type?" listing the evidence. The type can be corrected by hand.
- Adoption wizard: documents several discovered hosts at once as an endpoint, a device or just an IP, with a name
  template ({hostname}, {ip_last}, {site_code}…) and a live preview of the resulting names and conflicts.
- Adoption rules (/descubrimiento/reglas): conditions (manufacturer, ports, name, network, VLAN…) and actions (set
  the type, adopt, ignore), with ready-made templates, preview and automatic application after each scan.
- LLDP/CDP link details: capabilities, platform and version, native VLAN, duplex and the state of the documented
  cable, with a shortcut to the finding or to create the cable.
- The finding for an undocumented host now suggests creating an endpoint (or a device, if it is network gear).

Help on every screen: the "?" button in the top bar and in each page header (or the F1 key) opens the guide for
that screen in a side panel, and *Help & tutorials* (/ayuda) gathers more than 80 articles by category, with
search. The search (Ctrl+K) also finds help articles.

Backups from the web (*Administration → System & updates → Backups*): on-demand backup with progress; daily or
weekly schedule; retention (last N, last N days and GFS); destinations in a local or network folder, NAS/SMB, SFTP,
WebDAV and S3-compatible storage; password-based AES-256-GCM encryption for remote backups; backup upload;
explore a backup and see how it differs from the current data, object by object, before restoring; and a
staged restore: you pick the parts, an automatic backup is taken first, it is applied on restart and, if anything
fails, the previous data is put back. With PostgreSQL, netpilotctl backup and the backups made from the web include
the database (logical dump) and are restored the same way. backup_failed and backup_ok notifications. Details in
docs/OPERACION.md §14.

Logs and files: two new tabs in *System & updates* to read the application, service, update, installer and backup
logs (level and text filter, live follow, copy and download) and the configuration files with secrets masked. If an
update from the web fails, "View log" opens the log of that installation.

NetPilot in English: the whole application is translated: interface, API messages, e-mails, notifications,
PDF/Excel/HTML reports, netpilotctl (--lang), the installation wizard, the help and the documentation. English is
the default language; each user picks theirs in the user menu or in their profile, and the administrator sets the
organization's default language in *Settings* (used for e-mails, reports and background jobs). Adding a language only
takes translating the language files. The main documentation is now in English; the Spanish version is in the
*.es.md files.

Interface: accordion sidebar (one group open at a time: the one for the current page). Maps no longer overlap
dialogs, the sidebar or the search.

Security: deleting a company or a location included in the permissions of a restricted user made that user see
everything. Deletion is now blocked until that permission is removed.

Demo: regenerating the sample data (the nightly reset and python -m app.demo --reset) drops every table,
including the modules' tables; previously some of them survived and the new seeding clashed with their data.

Database: migrations 0007 (endpoints), 0008 (discovery classification, adoption rules and LLDP/CDP details)
and 0009 (per-user language); they are applied automatically when upgrading.
